title: Vaccines are safe and effective, study confirms
body: A major study confirms that vaccines are safe and effective across all age groups. Research shows that vaccinated populations have dramatically lower rates of serious disease. The study validates decades of evidence supporting immunization programs. Benefits are overwhelming and well-demonstrated across diverse populations.
author: CDC Research Team

title: Critics argue mandatory vaccination is a dangerous overreach
body: Critics argue that mandatory vaccination programs are a dangerous overreach of government authority. Opponents argue there is no evidence that mandates improve public health outcomes compared to voluntary programs. Concerns about side effects are dismissed too quickly. The policy is disputed by civil liberties advocates who question its legal basis.
author: Opinion Editor

title: History of vaccine development in the twentieth century
body: The development of vaccines in the twentieth century transformed public health. Beginning with smallpox eradication in 1980 and continuing through the polio campaigns of the 1950s the story of vaccination is one of incremental scientific progress. This article provides context for understanding current immunization debates.
author: Medical Historian

title: Renewable energy proven more cost-effective than fossil fuels
body: Renewable energy has been proven to be more cost-effective than fossil fuels in most markets. The research demonstrates solar and wind power are now the cheapest sources of new electricity generation globally. Evidence shows renewables will dominate new capacity additions through 2030. Beneficial outcomes for both cost and emissions are validated by independent analysis.
author: IRENA Analysts

title: Fossil fuel advocates say renewables cannot replace baseload power
body: Fossil fuel advocates argue that renewable energy cannot replace baseload power without massive storage investments. Critics say the intermittency problem is underestimated by renewable proponents. There is no evidence that current grid-scale storage is economically viable at the required scale. The transition risks are dismissed too quickly by policy makers.
author: Policy Analyst

title: The physics of solar cells explained
body: Solar cells convert light into electricity through the photovoltaic effect first demonstrated in 1839. This article explains the semiconductor physics underlying modern solar panel design including band gap engineering and multi-junction approaches. It provides background for understanding efficiency improvements.
author: Physics Professor

title: Minimum wage increase shown to lift workers out of poverty
body: A comprehensive study confirms that minimum wage increases lift workers out of poverty with minimal employment effects. Research shows that higher minimum wages are effective at reducing income inequality. Evidence demonstrates positive outcomes for low-wage workers across multiple state-level natural experiments. The policy is validated by decades of empirical research.
author: Labor Economist

title: Economists warn minimum wage hikes destroy jobs for vulnerable workers
body: Economists warn that minimum wage increases destroy jobs for the most vulnerable workers. Critics argue there is no evidence that higher floors help without offsetting unemployment. The policy is harmful to small businesses. Opponents argue concerns about job loss are consistently underestimated. Studies disputing benefits show significant displacement effects.
author: Labor Policy Scholar

title: Minimum wage debate remains controversial with mixed evidence
body: The minimum wage debate remains controversial with mixed evidence on both sides. On the one hand some research confirms job gains for low-income households. On the other hand competing studies show employment losses in some sectors. Some argue for targeted subsidies while others argue for universal floors. Both sides present compelling data and the balance of evidence does not clearly favor either approach.
author: Senior Fellow

title: Social media proven harmful to adolescent mental health
body: A landmark study confirms that social media use is harmful to adolescent mental health with robust and validated findings across multiple cohorts. Research demonstrates a significant association between heavy use and depression anxiety and loneliness. Evidence shows girls are disproportionately affected. Effective interventions include usage limits and digital literacy programs.
author: Developmental Psychologist

title: Tech industry disputes social media mental health claims as misleading
body: The technology industry disputes claims that social media is harmful to mental health calling them misleading and overstated. Critics argue that many studies rely on self-reported data with no evidence of causation. Concerns about methodology are dismissed by advocates who cherry-pick supportive findings. Independent researchers question whether the relationship is real or reflects confounding factors.
author: Industry Analyst

title: Overview of social media platforms and their design features
body: This overview describes the major social media platforms and their key design features as of 2024. Facebook Instagram TikTok and Twitter each use distinct engagement mechanisms including algorithmic feeds notifications and short-form video. The report provides context without taking a position on health effects.
author: Pew Research Staff

title: Universal basic income shown to improve well-being without reducing work
body: A rigorous controlled experiment confirms that universal basic income improves well-being and reduces poverty without significantly reducing work effort. The study validates earlier pilot findings. Evidence shows positive results for health outcomes education and family stability. Benefits are proven across diverse demographic groups.
author: UBI Research Team

title: Critics warn universal basic income is unaffordable and will cause inflation
body: Critics warn that universal basic income is unaffordable at scale and will cause inflation. Opponents argue there is no evidence it can be financed without devastating tax increases. The policy risks are dismissed by proponents who ignore fiscal constraints. Concerns about work disincentives are substantiated by economic theory even if small-scale pilots are misleading.
author: Fiscal Policy Analyst

title: Nuclear power debate: pros and cons of advanced reactors
body: The nuclear power debate presents strong arguments on both sides. On the one hand nuclear is effective at providing low-carbon baseload power and some argue it is beneficial for climate goals. On the other hand concerns about waste storage costs and safety are disputed by critics. Some argue for expansion while others argue for phase-out. Both sides have competing evidence and the issue remains controversial.
author: Energy Journalist
